newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurdish factions in northern Iraq fighting.
newsitem.headline: Kurdish factions in northern Iraq fighting.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish faction said on Monday it had clashed with a rival group in northern Iraq at the weekend as part of sporadic fighting that broke out earlier in April.
Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) representative Shazad Saib told Reuters his group had fought members of the Kurdistan Islamic Movement in the Halabja area, near the Iranian border.

Fighting flared again on Saturday despite mediation attempts after clashes between the two militias earlier this month. "There have been dozens of injured on both sides" since clashes began on April 6, Saib said.
He had no information on the number of injuries in the current wave of fighting.
Saib said PUK's traditional rival the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) was supporting the Islamist group.
The KDP and PUK have met frequently for peace talks in Ankara since they declared a ceasefire last October following intense fighting.
Kurdish rebels have been in control of northern Iraq since Baghdad's defeat in the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
Iraqi troops and tanks helped the KDP seize the key city of Arbil from the PUK last August. The United States fired misiles at southern Iraq in retaliation for Baghdad's involvement.
